evals.name: documentation-flag-correction
evals.prompt: Using the fixture, write a proposed PR title followed by only the reviewer-facing body prose that comes after the already-valid Diff disclosure. Do not use tools.
evals.expected_output: A concrete repository-conforming title and tiny, preservation-safe explanation state the exact correction and observed verification without importing a larger section structure, manual plan, or visual.
expectations: Explains the exact user-visible correction and preserves the still-current issue link without inventing broader impact.
Proposes a concrete Conventional Commit title centered on correcting the documented dry-run flag spelling without overstating the one-line documentation scope.
Uses a short paragraph or at most three bullets plus verification instead of a multi-section narrative.
Adds no manual operational plan, diagram, rollout, risk, or approval rhetoric unsupported by this documentation-only diff.

evals.name: preview-server-port-selection
evals.prompt: Using the fixture, draft the reviewer-facing PR body prose that follows the already-valid Diff disclosure. Do not use tools.
evals.expected_output: A concise straightforward body explains why ephemeral ports matter, states the narrow contract, and uses the author-validated parallel allocation comparison as the core manual path before clearly classified variants and cleanup.
expectations: Connects the change to parallel local and CI previews, defines the narrow port-zero and printed-URL contract, and avoids sales language.

Uses the two-process parallel allocation comparison as the shortest coherent core for this fixture's collision-avoidance claim, with commands, intended result, and the non-obvious quality signal; keeps required cleanup for every core-created server in that core or ends the scenario with literal `Cleanup gap:` when the supplied evidence leaves cleanup unresolved; and does not turn that evidentiary gap into a readiness gate because the fixture establishes none.

Keeps the single-process lifecycle as the orthogonal variant after the defining parallel-allocation core; begins that non-core scenario's heading or bullet with literal `Optional` because the fixture identifies no readiness gate; does not derive a readiness blocker from any cleanup gap; and does not imply that reviewers should repeat every author-run scenario.

Distinguishes author-run manual evidence from automated test evidence, ends every executed stateful scenario with literal `Cleanup:` or `Cleanup gap:` (or an explicit reference to a named shared cleanup), and does not claim an unrun host-mutating scenario.
Does not infer an issue-closing relationship from pull request number 42 or invent any unsupplied issue link.
Uses prose instead of a diagram because the behavior is a single local command path.

evals.name: command-envelope-stack
evals.prompt: Using the fixture, draft the complete reviewer-facing PR body prose after the already-valid Stack and Diff disclosures. Do not use tools.
evals.expected_output: A proportionate stacked-PR narrative makes the current command-envelope boundary reviewable, separates Before / This PR / Later ownership, routes review around generated noise, uses one focused visual only if it shortens comprehension, and presents bounded operational testing.
expectations: Answers why this slice is needed, why it belongs at this stack position, what is deliberately excluded, how to review it efficiently, and why the retained compatibility seam is maintainable.
Separates before, this PR, and later behavior without claiming future stack work as current behavior.
Provides a concrete review order centered on the command contract, producers, consumer, compatibility seam, and evidence while de-emphasizing generated schema noise.

Uses at most one focused command-flow visual when it shortens comprehension, while clear Before / This PR / Later prose or a table may pass without defending the absence of a visual; preserves the current direct adapter separately from the future envelope migration; rejects decorative whole-platform topology; and does not escalate beyond Mermaid without a concrete semantic, theming, or legibility need.

Centers the core on successful submission, API parity, replay, and the stored result because all four establish this fixture's shared-contract and idempotency claims; begins only the remaining orthogonal retry and destructive-reset scenario headings or bullets with literal `Optional` because the fixture identifies no readiness gate; states expected and non-obvious outcomes and the purge blast radius; ends every executed stateful scenario with literal `Cleanup:` or `Cleanup gap:` (or an explicit reference to a named shared cleanup) rather than treating cleanup as Optional; and does not derive a readiness blocker from a cleanup gap because the fixture establishes none.
Makes clear which evidence the author already gathered and does not pressure reviewers to rerun the entire matrix.
Does not infer an issue-closing relationship from pull request or stack numbers or invent any unsupplied issue link.

evals.name: provider-plugin-framework
evals.prompt: Using the fixture, respond to the request for an approval-ready PR title and body. Do not use tools.
evals.expected_output: The agent declines approval-ready marketing around an unsupported abstraction, identifies the consequential product/design decision, and recommends a truthful draft or authorized narrowing and validation before an approval case.
expectations: Does not produce persuasive approval framing that hides the unused abstraction, broad permissions, missing evidence, or duplicated path.

States that the change is not ready for approval rhetoric; offers truthful draft blockers or routes authorized implementation work back to narrowing, redesign, or evidence; and does not assume authority to mutate the change.
Surfaces one consequential scope or execution-authority decision and uses one-decision grilling semantics instead of bundling several unresolved choices or silently choosing.
Explains the blocker directly and respectfully without condescension, apology, or salesmanship.

evals.name: chat-only-draft
evals.prompt: Using the fixture, respond as the agent handling this request: "Draft a better pull request title and body here in chat. Do not change GitHub." Write the proposed title, the reviewer-facing body prose that follows the already-valid Diff disclosure, and your final user-facing status. Do not use tools.
evals.expected_output: A complete unpublished proposal pairs a concrete Conventional Commit title with a template-conforming body covering the exact pushed diff and observed verification, then ends with a chat-only status that performs and plans no preimage capture or GitHub mutation.
expectations: Proposes a concrete Conventional Commit title and a Summary, Changes, Verification, and Follow-up body that explains the retry-ledger change and its observed test verification without inventing scope.
Performs and plans no GitHub mutation: no preimage capture, no create or edit action, no ready-state action, and no handoff to publication as the active workflow.
Presents the proposal as an unpublished chat draft and does not claim that any stored title, body, or state changed.
Keeps the body proportional to the two-file implementation-and-test diff without a manual plan, diagram, rollout, risk, or approval rhetoric.

evals.name: config-loader-precedence
evals.prompt: Using the fixture, draft the reviewer-facing PR body prose that follows the already-valid Diff disclosure. Do not use tools.
evals.expected_output:
Reviewer-facing prose that states the precedence change, the operator problem it solves, and the observed evidence, with every paragraph and list item on one source line and any intended intra-item break written as an explicit
.
expectations: Places each paragraph and each list item on a single source line of unrestricted length rather than wrapping prose to a column budget, even though the fixture it reads is wrapped.
States the new resolution order and that the project file no longer overrides an environment variable, without inventing precedence sources absent from the fixture.
Reports the observed override, project-file, and default outcomes as evidence and keeps the operator migration note as separately tracked remaining work.
